newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PUMA sees tighter Australian mortgage bond pricing.
newsitem.headline: PUMA sees tighter Australian mortgage bond pricing.

text.p: Puma Management Limited, the securitisation arm of Macquarie Bank, believes mortgage backed securities (MBS) should achieve even better pricing in domestic and offshore markets than seen to date.

"The rationale for this is that Australian MBS are high credit assets and have a higher credit rating than the institutions which determine the bank bill curve. MBS should not incur a cost of funds greater than the bank curve," said PUMA Management Managing director Tony Gill.
PUMA's P-6 transaction in February had a record low weighted average margin over time of 16.6 basis points.
Gill said debt should be priced on the basis of its credit rating.

"If the credit rating is indicative of a capacity to pay on a timely basis, and AA and A entities are susceptible to a change in economic circumstances that AAA entities, then perhaps a premium should be paid by lower rated entities," Gill added.
